questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities (e.g. Courses, Internships...)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everything was handled digitally, which made it very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Assistance by the International Relations Officer and the Study Coordinator by sending out emails with all the necessary information.

No housing assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult. I found it through the usual websites for rentals in Sweden.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a lot more expensive than living on campus. However, experience from friends shows that the on campus living can be not up to our standards (mood on beds etc.)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I sent in an excel sheet with the courses that I wanted to register to. Then I would get a reply shortly before the start of the program (a bit too shortly in my opinion) of the courses that I would take. 

Shortly before the start of each course you would have to register for the course again on Ladok. That was a bit confusing, as I didn't expect to have to register again.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of help from the Study Coordinator of the Program. They are always a good address for help regarding problems with courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get one of the courses that I wanted, as it is a mandatory course for multiple programs and spots are limited. However that was communicated to me beforehand.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If possible, find out who the study coordinator of your program there is, and call or email them. They can help you in choosing your courses and also know about spot limitations  / how likely it is to get into the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level was more difficult than at the Uni of Copenhagen. The coordination of the courses was very well and the courses were small. Overall, the level of teaching was very high and I learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. However, there were more exercises and also a written exam, while at UCPH oral exams are more the norm.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Marine Sciences: Applied Project (Internship) 15 ECTS

Physical Oceanography II 15 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Physical Oceanography I and II because they give a very strong background in Physical Oceanography. However only to student with a lot of physics background.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food in general was very expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruits and vegetables are quite expensive in the winter. Food at the University is very expensive (> 70 DKK for lunch meal).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are sport clubs and many (social) activities specifically tailored to international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try out the activities for international students. They are well organised and offer cultural insight and new connections.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Spend a lot of time in nature, specifically the islands near Gothenburg. Also spend time in museums, other cultural activities and do sports, especially in the winter as it gets very dark.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, as it is similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
It was very difficult to make connections with locals, as Swedes tend to stay with their friends. 
If somebody invites you for lunch etc. definitely say yes! Try to talk to people in your class, as you already have something in common. It is very difficult to make friends with locals outside of that. Other internationals will be more open to connecting with you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The Swedish efficiency and organisation. 
Fika.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find housing fast, preferably through the University.
Don't have too high expectations on making friends with Swedes, it is more likely you will be friends with other internationals.
Prepare for an even darker winter.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic part, as my courses were great.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The darkness in the Winter. 
Socialising with local students.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
